title: Newborn weight loss: how much is normal?
summary: Most babies lose a little weight after birth, then regain it as feeding ramps up.
whatsNormal:
It is normal for full-term newborns to lose weight in the first days of life.

• Many lose up to about 7–10% of birth weight in the first week
• Weight loss often peaks around day 3–4, then trends back up
• Regaining birth weight by day 10–14 is a common benchmark
• Frequent feeding and good wet diapers help weight climb

Your pediatrician plots weight on a growth chart at visits, that context matters more than one number at home.
watchFor: Weight loss beyond what your clinician discussed at the hospital or first visit
Fewer wet diapers than expected after day 4
Very sleepy baby who will not wake for feeds
No swallowing or satisfied periods after feeds
callDoctorIf: You were told to recheck weight sooner, follow that plan
Signs of dehydration: sunken soft spot, dry mouth, no wet diapers 12+ hours after day 3
You are worried about feeding or weight, lactation support and a weight check can help
